findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an HTTP Request ('HTTP Response Splitting')
findings.trigger: If 'path' contains '\r\n' or '\n', it could inject additional headers or manipulate the HTTP request.
findings.assumptions: The 'path' parameter is derived from user input or an external source.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: If 'url', 'port', or 'wordlist_path' contains malicious input, it could lead to command injection.

findings.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound

findings.assumptions: The 'port' parameter is derived from user input or an external source.
